title: Functions Between Sets
short: A function assigns each element of its domain exactly one element of its codomain; the range is the set of outputs actually reached.
trouble: Students use "codomain" and "range" as if they meant the same set.

blocks.html: In algebra a function was usually a formula, and you found its domain and range. In discrete math a function can be any rule between sets: from people to birthdays, from strings to lengths, from a set to itself. The definition focuses on what makes something a function at all.

A function $f : A \to B$ assigns to each element of the domain $A$ exactly one element $f(a)$ of the codomain $B$. The range (or image) is the set of outputs actually reached, $f(A) = \{f(a) : a \in A\}$; it is a subset of the codomain and can be much smaller.

"Exactly one" has two parts: every element of $A$ gets an output (none is skipped), and no element gets two. In an arrow diagram, that means exactly one arrow leaves each dot of $A$; the dots of $B$ may receive any number of arrows, including none. The codomain is part of the definition, a promise about where outputs are allowed to land, while the range records where they actually land. Keeping the two apart is what makes the next lesson's idea of "onto" possible.

blocks.name: disc-relation
blocks.cap: An arrow diagram. Each element of $A$ needs exactly one arrow out. Switch the codomain to "outputs only" and notice that the elements never hit disappear: those form the difference between codomain and range.

blocks.title: Function or not?
steps: (i) Each of $1, 2, 3$ has exactly one output. Two inputs share the output $a$, which is allowed: a function.
(ii) $3$ has no output: not a function from $A$.

blocks.title: Range versus codomain
blocks.q: Let $f : \{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ be $f(x) = x^{2}$. Find the range.
steps: Range: $\{0, 1, 4\}$. The codomain is still $\mathbb{Z}$; most integers are simply never reached.

blocks.title: Counting functions
blocks.q: How many functions are there from $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ to $B = \{a, b\}$?
steps: Each of the $3$ elements of $A$ independently chooses one of $2$ outputs.
Product rule: $2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 2^{3} = 8$. In general there are $|B|^{|A|}$ functions from $A$ to $B$.

blocks.html: Treating codomain and range as the same set. For $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, $f(x) = 2x$, the codomain is $\mathbb{Z}$, but the range is only the even integers. Saying "the range is $\mathbb{Z}$" claims that $3$ is an output, and it is not. Check: the codomain is given in the arrow $f : A \to B$; the range you must work out by asking which outputs actually occur.
